question: Can the 2011 Naujan Lake National Park site profile support a waterbody-resolved MIMAROPA fish data batch?

source.title: Naujan Lake National Park Site Assessment and Profile Updating
source.access: The publisher-hosted PDF was downloaded to a temporary local review path and visually checked on PDF pages 150-151 (printed pages 130-131). No full table transcription or table-cell matrix was added to the repository.

waterbodies: 15 named tributaries in the report's sampling table
studyScope.samplingDesign: The methods describe 13 Naujan Lake sampling points (10 near/on shore and 3 central), 3 Butas River sites, and 15 tributaries. The river current limited exploration of the park reach. Macatoc River coordinates were mapped, but the report says high water prevented sampling there.
methods: hook and line with earthworm bait
studyScope.voucherHandling: The methods say collected specimens were brought to the laboratory for identification and voucher specimens deposited at the UPLB Museum of Natural History; accession numbers were not found in the reviewed passage.

reportedResults.parkWideFishRichnessClaim: The report describes a 2011 survey of 29 fish species, 26 genera and 17 families across Naujan Lake National Park.
reportedResults.lakeAndButasTable: The printed table contains 26 source-name rows and totals of 25 for Naujan Lake and 22 for Butas River. Its narrative separately states 20 lake species and 22 Butas River species. The difference is unresolved.
reportedResults.tributaryTable: The tributary table reports 19 source-name rows across 15 named tributaries. The narrative says three taxa occurred in all surveyed tributaries.
reportedResults.selectedTaxonCrosswalk: Compared the 13 source names in the 2024 Lake Naujan assessment: 11 have a source-name or current-combination match in the 2011 lake/Butas table, and nine of the 13 have one or more positive markers in the tributary table. The genus-only Carassius entry does not establish Carassius auratus. The full cell matrix is not retained; see mimaropa-naujan-2011-gilles-2024-locality-crosswalk-20261105.json.
reportedResults.dietMaterial: The profile lists a feeding-habit table for fishes, but its evidence basis and individual prey observations were not audited in this pass. No natural-diet claim or bait recommendation is extracted.

limits: The 2011 results are historical survey evidence, not proof of present-day occurrence, abundance, or catchability.
The report's 20-versus-25 lake count and other richness summaries are internally inconsistent; do not silently reconcile them.
Historical source-name forms, genus-only identifications, and rank/status claims require current taxonomic review; no source name is silently replaced or reidentified.

The selected historical taxon crosswalk has no fish-specific coordinates or station assignments. Named tributary columns do not by themselves provide taxon-linked coordinates. Macatoc River is explicitly an unsampled mapping lead.
The report discusses management and fishing conditions from its publication period; these are not current rules or safety alerts.

The front matter states copyright is held by MBCFI, all rights reserved, and reproduction for resale or other commercial purposes requires express written permission. No open license or app-specific reuse permission was verified.
The MBCFI profile is a separate historical source from NFRDI's July 2025-June 2026 Lake Naujan assessment; their totals must not be merged.
nextAction: Seek clarification of the conflicting lake totals, fish-survey dates, voucher accessions and app reuse terms from MBCFI/UPLB. In parallel, request NFRDI's 2025-2026 taxon/station data and reuse terms and continue reviewing independently reusable MIMAROPA sources.
